correctness.rationale: For trace-free complex symmetric A, probability-spherical fourth moments yield source norm 2||A||_F²/[d(d+2)] and each equator norm [2||A||_F²-4||row_i(A)||²+3|A_ii|²]/(d²-1). Their sum splits under coordinate sign flips into three off-diagonal sectors, plus the spectrum {1,0,(d-k)/d} of the selected-coordinate projection compressed to diagonal trace-zero vectors. Every multiplicity and all boundary dimensions are accounted for; injectivity for k>=3 and explicit rank failure for k<=2 follow. Two selected axes give a universal min-eigenvalue witness under arbitrary weights; spectral extrema inequalities under coordinate averaging prove optimal uniform weights. Direct Gram matrix checker passed 670 independent assertions. Finite numerical results are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A minimal number of mutually orthogonal codimension-one section scans is a natural observation design for fixed-band spherical quadrupole fields. The full spectrum in all d and k (not only rank), exact dimension-independent sharp condition sqrt(3) for three equators in d>=5, and universal optimality/unique lower-bound weighting make an exact self-contained reconstruction theorem. The result distinguishes function-valued traces from scalar Funk means and supplies explicit stability and optimizer equality cases; this is not a renaming, arbitrary finite enumeration, or unsupported downstream theorem. Its limitation to pure quadratics and orthogonal equators is explicitly stated.
